page: Amazon Web Services x8g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. It features an arm64 architecture with 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 390.87 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 175.81 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing and database operations both rank in the top tier, with database operations achieving 46,855.81 points. Geekbench multi-core performance is also in the top tier at 21,432.0 points, while single-core CPU benchmarks from stress-ng and Geekbench fall into the average range. Redis SET operations perform strongly at 66.43 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 71.55 GB/sec.

The server exhibits specific performance tradeoffs, particularly in large-language model inference where text generation for small models and prompt processing for large models are categorized as weak. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. Given the high memory-to-core ratio and top-tier database and memory bandwidth benchmarks, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
